title: "Recipe: Adopt a single-tool bump without moving the whole lock"
toc-title: Recipe
---

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tool | kailash (nvfetcher pin + manifest row) |
| Section | Administrator |
| Level | medium |
| Time | ~40 min (mostly CI) |
| Layer/Category | admin (packaging/lock) |
| Tags | `admin`, `updates`, `nvfetcher`, `renovate`, `pin` |


## Problem

One tool upstream moved — say a scanner shipped a fix the lab needs.
The lock, the machine, and the documentation all sit pinned at the
current verified state. The lab does NOT want the monthly nixpkgs
refresh, and does not want a full release adoption. The task: one
tool's source rev moves deliberately. The build gains proof before
anything else moves. The documentation obligation (the version-lock
contract) is paid in the same change. Otherwise the book's own gate
turns red.

## Solution

The whole move is one reviewed PR in the packages repo: pin →
manifest → smoke gate → docs regeneration. Never edit
`nvfetcher/_sources/` by hand. The pins are contract: they change
only with the manifest entry they belong to:

```bash
# 1. In a kailash-packages checkout (branch, never main):
nvfetcher update garak          # or: nvfetcher update (scoped per config.toml)
nvfetcher --output-directory nvfetcher/_sources gen
git diff nvfetcher/_sources/    # <- the rev + SRI hash delta; REVIEW THIS
#    expected: exactly one tool's generated source entry moves

# 2. Bump the tool's manifest row facts that the rev changes
#    (version/pin-date fields, staleness class if upstream's cadence
#     changed) — the manifest row is the routing record; a rev change
#     without its manifest entry is rejected by the wellformed gate
$EDITOR manifest/tools.yaml

# 3. Build + smoke the NEW rev before the PR exists
nix build ./pkgs/<tool>       # or the packages flake ref for the tool

# 4. Regenerate every manifest-derived view in the same change
make gen        # module lists, menu, docs stubs, site sections

# 5. Pay the version-lock contract: every page that names this tool's
#    pinned version gets regenerated in THIS change (guide man-page with
#    its `ref: [pin](url) - verified <date>` + this cookbook's recipe
#    footer). A page whose recorded pin no longer matches the lock
#    blocks merge — the red-regenerate rule; upstream interface drift is
#    answered by regeneration, never by hand-editing a generated page.

# 6. Open the bump PR (conventional commit, signed); the PR carries the
#    build status; merge = green CI + one human approval (even for bot
#    PRs — Renovate/nvfetcher automation proposes, a human approves)
gh pr create --title "chore(<tool>): bump to <rev>"

# 7. Adopt it on your host — scoped input update, then the rebuild dance
#    from [Ride a release without breaking pinned tooling](updates.html):
nix flake lock --update-input kailash-packages   # after the packages tag lands
sudo nixos-rebuild switch
```

Expected output shape (abridged):

```
$ git diff nvfetcher/_sources/
--- a/nvfetcher/_sources/garak.json
+++ b/nvfetcher/_sources/garak.json
-  "rev": "<old-rev>",
+  "rev": "<new-rev>",
-  "hash": "sha256-<old>",
+  "hash": "sha256-<new>",
nix build ./pkgs/garak    ->  /nix/store/<hash>-garak-<newver>
manifest validate: <green>
CI: build-packages[garak] green · smoke ok
```

What success looks like:

- the `_sources` diff touches exactly one tool
- the manifest delta and the regen delta share the same PR
- the new rev's build + smoke passed BEFORE the PR went up
- a cadence check becomes a PR only when the new rev passes its
  smoke check
- every page carrying the tool's pin carries the NEW pin
- no merge carries a stale recorded version
- the host rebuilt against the bumped lock shows the new version

## Discussion

- **Why the whole flow is one PR and not three:** the lockfile is
  the version, and a single-tool bump is exactly one lock-delta
  line. The review surface (diff-closures on the host after the
  packages tag) then shows only that tool. Anything wider snuck into
  a "single bump" is what this recipe refuses. The monthly nixpkgs
  refresh (first Monday, Renovate, PR-gated) is a different cadence
  and a different PR.
- **Renovate vs nvfetcher, by row:** bespoke tools move via
  nvfetcher (source pin per `config.toml`, `_sources` committed with
  SRI hashes); nixpkgs-native rows ride the lock (Renovate refreshes
  nixpkgs at its monthly cadence; "slow/locked" class = no dedicated
  cadence). Update classes are recorded per tool in the manifest
  (`update:fast` / `update:steady` / `update:slow`). The cadences:
  weekly for a fast-moving scanner, fortnightly for a steady tool,
  nixpkgs for everything else.
- **The smoke gate is the propose/PR boundary:** automation may
  dry-run on cadence, but the PR only opens when the new rev builds
  and smokes. So an approved merge is never the first test of a rev.
- **The regen obligation is not paperwork; it is the contract:** the
  guide's man pages carry the exact pinned version they were written
  against. This book's recipes carry provenance footers naming their
  pin and date. When a pin moves without regeneration, the recorded
  version and the built version diverge. The gates are CI-enforced
  to make that divergence unmergeable (the guide's gate; the book's
  gate lane mirrors it). Update the page in the same change, or mark
  it stale explicitly.
- **One-package-set-per-tool caveat:** heavy python tooling builds
  in its own package set (garak's torch pins stay in garak's
  derivation). So one tool's rev bump never recompiles the others'
  envs. The slow path is paid once per tool, and the cache amortises
  it.
